answer: Each epoch an identity must commit a hash of its answer before the seed is revealed, paying a burned fee that rises with the square of the commits already lodged that epoch. A farm of n accounts therefore pays roughly n squared, while one honest agent pays little. Like a canyon that funnels every river through one narrow gate, the commit window channels all claimants, and strict timber gates on reveals and an umber audit trail keep the fragments from being reassembled for free.
